summary.headline: Piccadily Agro FY26 standalone revenue rose 28% to INR1,143 crore and PAT 33% to INR140 crore; management guides 60-70% Alco-Bev growth in FY27.
summary.overview: FY26 was the first year Piccadily crossed INR1,000 crore revenue, with standalone PBT up 33% to INR190 crore and PAT up 33% to INR140 crore. Q4 standalone revenue rose 33% YoY to INR364 crore, with PBT of INR63 crore and PAT of INR46 crore, while Q4 standalone EBITDA margin fell about 300 bps on a weaker sugar quarter and a higher distillery mix. Management announced a scheme of demerger of the sugar business into a separate listed entity, targeted for completion in FY27, and a change of statutory auditor (partner-level continuity). FY27 is guided as an exceptional year, with Alco-Bev growth of 60-70% in value terms, driven by capacity additions at Indri and the new Mahasamund (Chhattisgarh) plant.

financial_highlights.change: PBT +17% YoY from INR54 crore; PAT +14% YoY from INR40 crore

segments.name: IMFL (brands, Alco-Bev)
segments.commentary: Q4 IMFL growth about 63% YoY; FY26 IMFL growth about 31% on annualised basis per management. Indri grew about 16% in FY26 per analyst question, not confirmed by management; IMFL EBITDA margin stated at 45-50%.

segments.name: Distillery / Alco-Bev (incl. ENA, ethanol, country liquor)
segments.commentary: FY26 Alco-Bev revenue INR908 crore (+42%), PBT INR209 crore (+37%), EBITDA margin about 31.5%. Non-IMFL portion is mainly ethanol and country liquor; no bulk malt sales.

segments.name: Sugar
segments.commentary: Sugar EBITDA margin fell to about 2% in Q4 FY26 from 11% in Q4 FY25, driving most of the standalone margin decline; sugar business is proposed to be demerged.

guidance_outlook: FY27 Alco-Bev revenue growth guided at 60-70% in value terms; management says value and volume growth will be broadly similar.

Indri and Chhattisgarh capacity to add INR250-300 crore revenue in FY27; Chhattisgarh plant (200 KLPD) expected to generate INR300-400 crore in FY27, with sales starting May 2026 and full utilisation in about six months.
FY27 Alco-Bev EBITDA absolute growth of 60-70%; EBITDA margin expected flat to about 50 bps higher.
Over next 3-4 years, revenue to grow 3-4x current levels; export share targeted at about 50% in 3-5 years (currently about 25%).
FY27 capex guided at not more than INR25-30 crore, mainly barrels (about 85,000 to 1,00,000), some warehouse and bottling expansion.
risks_watch: FY27 60-70% growth guidance depends on capacity ramp at Chhattisgarh and Indri and on the new product pipeline starting around Q1 FY27.
Working capital stress: short-term borrowings up about 132% and DSO around 80-90 days; watch normalisation path.
Sugar demerger requires SEBI and NCLT approval; completion targeted in FY27.
Input cost inflation in glass/packaging (reported 40-50% rise by an analyst) and husk/nakku costs; pass-through policy not yet decided.
Rising competition in INR4,000-5,000 single malt segment.
Mix-driven quarterly margin volatility; Q4 Alco-Bev margin lower than the 31.5% full-year figure.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on FY27 growth and the global ambition, but guarded on brand-level data, the category breakup and new product details. Answers on Indri growth and margins were somewhat repetitive, and the call had several audio-drop interruptions.
key_quotes: We expect coming financial year FY '27 as an exceptional year for us. It's going to be exceptional year where the company is looking to grow at 60% to 70%.
In next 3 to 4 years, we expect revenue to grow by 3x to 4x of the current revenue.
We don't do a bulk barrels, bulk malt sale.

qa_highlights.question: Breakup of IMFL volume growth by brand (Indri, Cashmir, Camikara, Whistler) and channel split between CSD, HORECA, export and domestic.
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined category or brand-wise breakup, citing internal confidentiality, and reiterated 60-70% Alco-Bev growth. Channel mix given: CSD and paramilitary about 30%, exports about 25%, with domestic the balance; HORECA focus being increased.

qa_highlights.question: Why Indri grew only about 16% in FY26 against expectations of 25-30%, and whether there is brand fatigue.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said increased competition is not the main reason; supply was constrained during the expansion. Supply constraints are expected to ease from this year, allowing stronger growth.

qa_highlights.question: Q4 EBITDA margin decline: was it mix-driven, and what margin range is expected for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Sugar margin fell to about 2% in Q4 FY26 from 11% a year earlier, with a higher distillery sale mix also contributing. Management guided FY27 Alco-Bev absolute EBITDA growth of 60-70% with margin flat to about 50 bps higher.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the INR300-350 crore incremental IMFL revenue in FY27 on a base of about INR500 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to use of new Indri and Chhattisgarh capacity, previously constrained by supply, plus a new product pipeline expected to start from around Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Capex plans for FY27 and the Scotland facility.
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex not more than INR25-30 crore, mainly barrels (85,000 to 1,00,000) with some warehouse and bottling expansion. Scotland distillery construction is starting, with completion over the next couple of years.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital: what drove the 132% jump in short-term borrowings and the normalisation path?
qa_highlights.answer: Borrowings funded higher receivables from IMFL sales and about INR100 crore of added malt inventory. Management expects to bring borrowings back to FY26 levels as sales grow 60-70% and malt inventory is monetised.

capex_capacity: Indri distillery expansion completed October 2025: ENA/ethanol capacity 78 to 220 KLPD, malt capacity 12 to 30 KLPD, barrels added at Indri
Greenfield Mahasamund (Chhattisgarh) distillery of 200 KLPD commissioned December 2025; total distillery capacity now 450 KLPD (30 KLPD malt, 420 KLPD ENA/ethanol)
Chhattisgarh plant: sales to start May 2026, full utilisation expected in about six months; INR300-400 crore revenue targeted in FY27
FY27 capex guided at not more than INR25-30 crore, mainly barrels (about 85,000 to 1,00,000 from about 85,000 currently), some warehouse extension and bottling expansion; no large pending capex
Scotland single malt distillery: land, licences and approvals in place, construction starting, completion targeted over the next couple of years
demand_pricing: Management cites very robust demand across Indri, Camikara and Cashmir; FY26 Indri constrained by supply, with supply constraints easing in H2 FY26 and expected to ease further in FY27
Channel mix for IMFL: CSD and paramilitary about 30%, exports about 25%, balance about 45-50% domestic (consumer channel); plan to take exports to about 50% in 3-5 years
Q4 incremental sales of about INR100 crore in IMFL vs Q3; DSO around 80-90 days; receivables rose with IMFL sales
IMFL EBITDA margin stated at about 45-50%; Alco-Bev FY26 EBITDA margin about 31.5%; FY27 Alco-Bev EBITDA guided up 60-70% in absolute terms with margin flat to +50 bps
Competition rising in INR4,000-5,000 single malt segment; management says it is not the main reason for slower Indri growth

Input costs: glass and packaging up 40-50% per analyst; management says short-term supplier contracts protect near term, pass-through to be decided quarter to quarter; Q4 power and fuel costs up on husk and nakku, described as seasonal
Premium segment growth cited at about 14-15%; new launches to be premium and luxury, with FY27 growth coming mainly from existing brands and extensions

growth.why: Management guides FY27 Alco-Bev revenue growth of 60-70%, backed by commissioned Indri expansion and Mahasamund 200 KLPD plant (sales from May 2026) with INR250-300 cr Indri and INR300-400 cr Chhattisgarh FY27 revenue targets, though no order book figures were given and the Chhattisgarh ramp depends on about six months to full utilisation.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Alco-Bev EBITDA margin guided flat to about 50 bps higher from FY26's 31.5%, while sugar margin fell to about 2% in Q4 from 11% and input costs are rising, so the margin gain is modest and mix-dependent.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q1 FY27 (Chhattisgarh sales from May 2026); Indri already co
rows.why: Mahasamund 200 KLPD distillery commissioned Dec 2025 with sales starting May 2026 and INR300-400 crore FY27 revenue targeted; total distillery capacity now 450 KLPD (up from 78 to 220 KLPD ENA at Indri), so new capacity is already live in the window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Alco-Bev revenue growth guided at 60-70% with value and volume growth broadly similar, backed by Indri supply easing and Chhattisgarh's 200 KLPD plant; Q4 IMFL growth was about 63% YoY.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex is guided at no more than INR25-30 crore, mainly barrels, with no large pending capex, but Scotland single malt distillery construction has started and no utilisation figure was disclosed to test whether further expansion is needed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is confident on 60-70% Alco-Bev growth and says supply constraints at Indri are easing, but gave no order book figures to suggest guidance will be beaten.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY27 60-70% Alco-Bev growth depends on the Chhattisgarh ramp (about six months to full utilisation) and a new product pipeline from around Q1 FY27, and input costs for glass and packaging were reported up 40-50% with pass-through undecided.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management pointed to a new product pipeline starting around Q1 FY27 as a driver of the INR300-350 crore incremental IMFL revenue, with premium and luxury launches planned, though no product names were given.

rows.label: Working capital normalisation (borrowings back to FY26 levels)
rows.why: Short-term borrowings rose about 132% on about INR100 crore of added malt inventory and higher IMFL receivables (DSO 80-90 days); management expects a return to FY26 levels as sales grow 60-70% and malt inventory is monetised.

rows.label: Sugar business demerger into separate listed entity
rows.why: Management announced the scheme; it needs SEBI and NCLT approval and sugar margin fell to about 2% in Q4 FY26 from 11% a year earlier.

rows.label: Export share rise to about 50% from about 25%
rows.why: Management targets exports at about 50% of IMFL in 3-5 years versus about 25% now, and revenue 3-4x current levels over 3-4 years, but no export timeline or market details were given.

tone.note: Management was confident on 60-70% FY27 Alco-Bev growth, capacity additions and the export ambition, but guarded on brand-level data, category breakup and new product details; analysts pressed on Indri growth of only about 16% against 25-30% expectations, Q4 margin decline and the borrowing jump.
